lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Management pre-guided Q3 (Jun-Aug) as seasonally softer, with about one week or 8% of production lost. On the Q2 run-rate of C$52.7M that implies roughly C$48.5M before growth, FX and defence ramp. Against a C$0.18 EPS bar (Q2 printed 0.20, Q3-25 0.11), my arithmetic (about C$50-51M revenue, about 34% GM, opex near Q2) gives EPS of about 0.15-0.17, and revenue below the snippet-only C$53M average.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (adj EBITDA down YoY despite +10% revenue): -10.89% (baseline, 2026-04-09). Q2 2026 record EPS 0.20 against a 0.16 bar: -3.03% (baseline, 2026-07-08). Q4 2025 (EPS 0.14 against 0.13): +6.71%.

findings.finding: The Canadian dollar was weaker through FTG's Q3. Bank of Canada USD/CAD averaged 1.404 in June, 1.411 in July and about 1.39 in August, against a Q2 average of 1.373 and a Q3-25 average of 1.372. That lifts CAD-reported revenue about 2% on a business with roughly 90% non-Canadian sales, and widens margin at the Canadian plants, which sell in USD with CAD costs. The period-end rate (about 1.387 on 08-28 against 1.380 on 05-29) also implies a small revaluation gain rather than Q2's C$0.3M loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX was a named headwind in Q1 2026 (C$1.3M revenue, C$0.7M FX loss in Circuits), and that print fell -10.89%. In Q2 FX was a smaller drag and the print fell -3.03%. There is no clean history of an FX-tailwind quarter.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said tariffs are now raising Circuits input costs, 'in the millions of dollars in 2026', with input costs 'moving up fast' and pass-through to customers only started. So Q2's record 36.5% gross margin (36.7% before FX) is unlikely to hold in a lower-volume Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 Circuits adj EBITDA fell from C$5.5M to C$4.0M on margin; the stock fell -10.89%. Q2 GM jumped to 36.5%, yet the stock still fell -3.03%.

findings.finding: Initial deliveries on the two classified defence PCB programs (CEO: C$50-100M a year of customer board spend in total) were scheduled to begin in Q3 2026, and opening POs are in a record C$193.5M backlog (book-to-bill 1.64). TTM Technologies' Q2 (quarter to 2026-06-29) showed A&D sales +14% YoY, a 1.49 company book-to-bill and a raised outlook, so bookings and backlog are likely strong again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 record bookings (+89%) and backlog (+30%): -3.03%. The backlog line has not been rewarded on the print day.

findings.finding: US 50% Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods took effect 2026-08-19, regardless of USMCA origin, with qualifying civil aircraft and parts exempt. On 2026-08-24 Canadian aerospace sold off (FTG -13.9% on 237k shares, Magellan -8.5%, TMX tape), and FTG has since fully recovered (18.76 to 24.80). The Q3 call is the first time the company comments on its exposure after the effective date, especially for Toronto-made PCBs, which may not count as 'aircraft parts'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-08-24 tariff-scare day: -13.9% with no company news, then a full recovery by late September.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is long and extended: +26.1% in 20 sessions, +112% YTD, about 40x trailing EPS, at the C$30 target of both brokers within roughly 20%. Short interest is only 1.28% (2.7 days to cover). This is a name whose two most recent prints were sold even on records.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Run-ups into the last two prints (Q2: 22.7 to 26.07 in the week before) were followed by -3.03% and -10.89% reactions (baseline history).

outside_window.finding: US Section 232 aerospace proclamation of 2026-07-09: no tariffs now, a 180-day negotiation window ending around early January 2027, tariffs reserved. Separately, US tariffs on Canadian autos and steel step up to 50% on 2027-01-01.

findings.finding: The sell-side bar of EPS 0.46-0.48 (+7-12% on 0.43) needs a Q3 EBITDA margin of roughly 11.8-12.0% against 11.4% a year ago. Richelieu's own disclosures show tariff pass-through diluting margin 20-30bp a year (Q1 9.3% vs 9.6%, Q2 10.6% vs 10.8%), and the CFO said on 2026-07-09 that there is 'nothing else' structurally. On revenue of about C$534M and a margin of 11.1-11.3%, EPS comes out at about 0.44-0.45, a miss of about 5%. Consensus has missed in 3 of the last 4 quarters by 10-13%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same-day moves off TMX bars around Richelieu's intraday releases: Q2 FY26 EPS 0.42 vs 0.47 (miss of about 11%) went -8.91% on 2026-07-09; Q1 FY26 0.26 vs 0.30 went -4.22% on 2026-04-09; Q4 FY25 in line went -1.41% (+2.03% over two days); Q3 FY25 beat of +4.9% went +4.51% (+8.23% over two days) on 2025-10-09. EPS surprises have moved this stock roughly 0.4-0.9x.

findings.finding: The full-year aim of an EBITDA margin 'close to 11%' (CFO, Q2 call) implies about 11.9% in H2, given 10.0% in H1 on C$995.6M of sales, against 11.5% in H2 FY25 with tariff dilution still running. The CFO already hedged it ('we would need a bit more rigor in the market'), and the Q3 call at 10:00 ET on 8 October is likely to walk it down to roughly 10.5-10.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Richelieu gives no formal numeric guidance; margin commentary is the guide. The Q2 call where the 11% was hedged coincided with the -8.91% day (2026-07-09), and both analysts cut their targets on 2026-07-13. That move cannot be split between the EPS miss and the margin commentary.

findings.finding: USD/CAD averaged 1.4019 in June-August 2026 against 1.3720 in June-August 2025 (Bank of Canada daily series), a +2.2% translation tailwind on the roughly 45% of sales made in the US. That is worth about +1.0pt of reported growth and reverses the -1.1pt FX drag in Q2 (average rate 1.373 vs 1.407).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has been a disclosed swing factor: Q1 FY26 EBITDA would have been +5.6% excluding FX against +1.9% reported, and that quarter went -4.22%. No clean episode isolates FX.

findings.finding: MasterBrand, the largest US cabinet maker and now owner of American Woodmark, reported a mid- to high-single-digit decline in the US cabinet market in its Q2 2026 (April-June) and forecasts a mid-single-digit decline in its 2026 addressable market. US cabinet manufacturers are Richelieu's core US customer base, and Richelieu's US manufacturers' internal growth was only +3.1% in Q2, partly from price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US manufacturers' line went from +7.3% internal in Q3 FY25 (tariff pricing; stock +4.51%) to +3.1% in Q2 FY26 (stock -8.91%). The deceleration has coincided with the weaker reactions.

findings.finding: Home Depot said Canada out-comped the company in its fiscal Q2 (May to 2 August 2026), with positive transactions and units, after a negative Q1. Canada is about 55% of Richelieu's sales, and its Canadian retailers' line was already +8.1% internal in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Canada grew +5.5% in Q2 FY26 (3.8% internal) and Quebec was up more than 10% in June, but the stock fell 8.91% on margin anyway. Canadian top-line strength has not carried the reaction.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-02 Richelieu bought Penrod's hardware division (about US$70M of annual sales, roughly 4.6% of group sales, US door hardware). It closed after the quarter, so it is outside the Q3 figures, but terms, financing and first-year contribution are likely to be given on the release or call. The Q3 balance sheet and call will also show the funding.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement on 2026-09-02 after the close was met with +2.47% on 2026-09-03 (34.45 to 35.30 on TMX bars). Acquisition-heavy releases have had mixed reactions.

findings.finding: IEEPA duties were struck down on 2026-02-20 (Learning Resources v. Trump), and CBP's CAPE refund module has been processing claims since 2026-04-20 (Phase 2 from 2026-06-29). Richelieu imports into the US through 73 US distribution centres and passed tariffs through to customers in dollars, so any refund it books as importer of record would be a windfall in a quarter. Neither the Q2 release nor the Q2 call mentions a refund, so whether one is booked in Q3 is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent on this name. A below-operating-income one-off with no path to the guide is sized at a fraction of operating-profit dollars.

outside_window.finding: The Drummondville distribution centre expansion (more than C$15M, from 40k to 180k sq ft) becomes operational in spring 2027. It is capex inside the C$18-20M guide and has no window effect.
